tender.title: Provision and Delivery of an Annual Town Centre Soapbox Racing Event 2027-2029
tender.description:
Kettering Town Council invites tenders from suitably capable event operators to plan, promote, manage and deliver an annual public soapbox racing event in Kettering town centre in 2027, 2028 and 2029.
The Council is seeking a safe, professionally managed and visually engaging event that attracts participants and spectators, supports town-centre footfall and creates a distinctive annual experience for Kettering.
The successful supplier will provide an end-to-end event management service. This will include event design and race operation; event planning and project management; participant recruitment, registration and race management; specialist race infrastructure; event safety, risk assessment and emergency planning; liaison in relation to traffic management, road closures and relevant permissions; marketing and audience development; and operational management and delivery of the event.
The supplier will be expected to work collaboratively with Kettering Town Council and relevant local stakeholders, including North Northamptonshire Council, event safety partners, land and highway stakeholders and emergency services where required.
The Council is also seeking an approach that considers accessibility, sustainability, community involvement and opportunities to support local businesses, organisations and traders where appropriate.
The contract will cover three annual events in 2027, 2028 and 2029, with an indicative budget of approximately £40,000 excluding VAT per event, giving an indicative three-year contract value of approximately £120,000 excluding VAT. Tenderers are required to identify VAT treatment and clearly state all assumptions, exclusions and potential additional charges.
Full details of the required services, Council and supplier responsibilities, minimum requirements, pricing schedule and evaluation methodology are contained within the Invitation to Tender.
tender.submissionMethodDetails:
Tender submissions must be made electronically in accordance with the requirements set out in the Invitation to Tender. The tender documents and full submission instructions are available at: https://www.ketteringtowncouncil.gov.uk/documents/2176303
Completed tenders must be submitted by email to anonymised@example.invalid by 12 noon on Friday 23 October 2026.
Tenderers are responsible for ensuring that their submission is received by the Council before the deadline. Late submissions may not be considered. Clarification questions must be submitted by 12 noon on Friday 9 October 2026 in accordance with the Invitation to Tender.

tender.description:
The Food Standards Agency (FSA) is an independent Government department working across England, Wales and Northern Ireland to protect public health and consumers wider interest in food.  We make sure food is safe and what it says it is. 
The FSA are looking to appoint a supplier to deliver a research project to undertake metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analyses of faecal samples generated as part of The Third Study of Infectious Intestinal Disease (IID3), alongside other relevant datasets. The contract will run for a period of 24 months, with an optional 6-month extension period if required. The maximum budget assigned for this project is £600,000, excluding VAT.

tender.title: UK_1003 Global Evaluation Framework Retender 2026
tender.description: The British Council is looking for multiple providers to join its 2026 Global Evaluation Framework. This framework will replace the 2022 Global Evaluation Framework, which is due to expire in 2026. This global framework will be the British Council's primary route for the procurement of monitoring and evaluation consultancy work. Suppliers who join the framework will be eligible to tender for monitoring and evaluation across the British Council's global operations.

frameworkAgreement.description:
A Lot 1 Framework Agreement will be considered for a maximum of 3 potential suppliers whose 
Proposal is supported by any required verification evidence (to include, without limitation, any updated 
information or references relating to any Exclusion Grounds or Conditions of Participation responses) 
obtained by the British Council relating to any self-certification or other requirements referred to in the 
Procurement Specific Questionnaire.
18.5.2 A Lot 2 Framework Agreement will be considered for a maximum of 70 potential suppliers whose 
Proposal is supported by any required verification evidence (to include, without limitation, any updated 
information or references relating to any Exclusion Grounds or Conditions of Participation responses) 
obtained by the British Council relating to any self-certification or other requirements referred to in the 
Procurement Specific Questionnaire. 
For Lot 1 and Lot 2, if any verification evidence requested from a supplier, or a relevant third party as 
may be referred to by the supplier in the Procurement Specific Questionnaire as a party prepared to provide 
such information, is not provided in accordance with any timescales specified by the British Council and/or 
any evidence reviewed by the British Council (whose decision shall be final) does not demonstrate 
compliance with any such requirement, the British Council may reject that tender response in full and 
disqualify the potential winning supplier from the Procurement Process at that point.
Thematic and Regional Tags (voluntary) - In addition to bidding to Lot 2, suppliers are invited to submit 
additional evidence of expertise across the different thematic areas and regions. Suppliers who submit 3 or 
more examples of relevant expertise in a specific thematic and regional areas will receive a corresponding 
thematic/regional "tag," denoting their documented expertise in this area. These voluntary responses will be 
submitted in Annex 6 (Lot 2 Thematic and Regional Tag(s) Response (Voluntary)).
Only the thematic and regional tag responses from the (up to) 70 suppliers selected for consideration 
will be reviewed. Tag responses will be reviewed independently of Annex 3 (Supplier Response). Each 
individual thematic or regional tag response will be reviewed independently of other tag submissions. 
Therefore, experience cited in either a) Annex 3 or b) other tag responses in Annex 6, should be cited again 
in supplier's responses for the relevant tag. This may mean citing an experience more than once. 
18.8 Tag responses will be scored as met/not met the tag requirement. A tag will be awarded for responses 
which meet the relevant tag's requirements as outlined in Annex 6.
It is anticipated that these tags will be used by the British Council to identify Lot 2 suppliers with 
specialist expertise. Suppliers may then be invited to bid for relevant specialist work either through a) mini
competitions when there are multiple suppliers with the relevant expertise or b) to submit proposals for direct 
awards, and addendums where there is only one supplier with the relevant expertise within the Lot. Where 
specialist expertise is not required or cannot be identified using tags, work will be procured via an open 
competition on Lot 2.
British Council ITT (Open Procedure) 
Revised Feb 2025
Suppliers can submit evidence for as many or as few thematic and regional tags as match their 
expertise-a supplier could bid to receive all or no tags, or any number in between. There is no cap on the 
number of suppliers who receive a tag.

tender.title: Recruitment Services for Deliberative Engagement
tender.description: The SPCB require a Contractor to provide recruitment services to randomly select and recruit members of the public to participate in deliberative engagement events delivered to support the work of the Scottish Parliament.

lots.description:
The SPCB require a Contractor to provide recruitment services to randomly select and recruit members of the public to participate in deliberative engagement events delivered to support the work of the Scottish Parliament.
Recruitment shall be undertaken using a robust and transparent random selection methodology, designed to minimise selection bias and maximise inclusivity. The preferred approach is random selection via postal invitation to a randomly generated sample of residential addresses, with appropriate follow-up procedures to support response rates and accessibility. Where alternative or supplementary methods are proposed, Contractors must clearly demonstrate how these preserve the integrity of random selection.
Potential participants will then be stratified from the pool of respondents to broadly reflect the specified demographic profile requested by the Scottish Parliament, such as the adult population of Scotland, a Parliamentary region, or within a specified radius of an event location. To ensure broad participation the contractor should consider how their methodology encourages participation from residents in lower SIMD and have contingency plans to support successful fulfilment of all demographic targets.
The SPCB will typically require between 20–30 participants to be involved in deliberative engagement processes; however, this may vary depending on the needs of the Parliamentary Committee requesting deliberative input and available budget.
The Contractor shall propose a methodology that is both cost-effective and consistent with the principles of random selection and stratified sampling, setting out how participants will be contacted, recruited, and selected from the respondent pool.

criteria.minimum:
The SPCB requires tenderers to have a Creditsafe Risk Score of 40 or higher to demonstrate satisfactory financial standing. If a tenderer has a lower credit risk score than 40 on Creditsafe and has the backing of a parent company with a credit risk score of 40 or higher, then the provision of a parent company guarantee will be required prior to the award of any contract. If a tenderer has a lower credit risk score than 40 and cannot provide a parent company guarantee, they must submit evidence to support a stable and improved financial standing with their tender or the tender may be rejected. If no evidence is provided with the tender or the evidence provided is not sufficient to demonstrate a satisfactory financial position to the satisfaction of the SPCB (whose decision in this regard shall be final), then the tender will be rejected and will not be evaluated further.
If a tenderer is not listed on Creditsafe, for whatever reason, then it will be asked to submit equivalent accounts to enable the required assessment of financial standing to be carried out.  If the information provided does not, in the SPCB’s opinion, demonstrate a satisfactory financial position, the bid may be rejected.
